extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards in the MPEP governing inventor oaths/declarations and related inventor/application information (including continuing applications, non-English oaths, signatures, inventorship corrections, and supplemental declarations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship determination in continuing applications (when no ADS filed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application data sheet is not filed before or concurrently with the copy of the inventor’s oath or declaration from the earlier-filed application, the inventorship is the inventorship set forth in the copy of the inventor’s oath or declaration from the earlier-filed application unless accompanied by a signed statement pursuant to 37 CFR 1.33(b) stating the name of each inventor in the continuing application (see 37 CFR 1.63(d)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new joint inventor named in the continuing application must provide an oath or declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63, except as provided in 37 CFR 1.64 (see MPEP §602.05(d)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior oath or declaration in continuations/divisionals filed before Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application filed before September 16, 2012 under 37 CFR 1.53(b) may be filed with a copy of the oath or declaration from the prior nonprovisional application (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63(d)(1)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copied oath/declaration omits signatures of one or more inventors, OPAP should send a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring the nonsigning inventor’s signature unless a copy of the decision according pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 is included. Applicant may reply with the missing signature and the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) for late filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English oaths and declarations (37 CFR 1.69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an individual making an oath or declaration cannot understand English, the oath or declaration must be in a language that such individual can understand and shall state that such individual understands the content of any documents to which the oath or declaration relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the non-English text is in a PTO-provided form or per PCT Rule 4.17(iv), it must be accompanied by an English translation and a statement that the translation is accurate. For oaths/declarations under §1.63, the translation may be filed within two months of notification. A single non-English oath may be accepted for joint inventors if all understand that language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor bibliographic information required in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration must include certain inventor bibliographic information: name(s) of inventor(s), and depending on filing date, residence, mailing address, and (for pre-Sept 16, 2012 filings) citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residence (city and either state or foreign country) is required unless included in an ADS (37 CFR 1.76). Mailing/post office address must be supplied if not in an ADS. For inventors in the U.S. Armed Services, a statement to that effect satisfies residence. Omissions will trigger OPAP notification to supply the omitted information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and execution formalities for inventor oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must be signed by each actual inventor (except as permitted under 37 CFR 1.64); there is no required form of signature and non-English characters, marks (attested by witness), or titles (e.g., 'Dr.') are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed through EFS-Web must contain an oath or declaration personally signed by the inventor. It is improper to sign an oath/declaration that is not attached to or does not identify the application. 'Attached' need not be literally fastened; physical proximity at execution is sufficient. Copies of declarations are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution on behalf of inventor (post- vs pre-Sept 16, 2012 rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, only inventors can execute an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63; substitute statements under 37 CFR 1.64 may be used in permitted circumstances. For applications filed before that date, statutory provisions (35 U.S.C. 116, 117, pre-AIA rules) allow joint inventors or legal representatives to sign on behalf of an absent, refusing, deceased, or incapacitated inventor under limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney may not sign an oath/declaration on behalf of the inventor unless the attorney has the proprietary interest required by the pre-AIA provisions; case law (e.g., Staeger, In re Striker) found attorney-signed oaths defective where attorney lacked proprietary interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor name requirements and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, 37 CFR 1.63 requires identification of the inventor by legal name. For applications filed before that date, pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63(a)(2) required full name including family name and at least one given name without abbreviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections or updates to an inventor’s name in a nonprovisional application must be made via 37 CFR 1.48(f) and must include an ADS (37 CFR 1.76) identifying each inventor by legal name and the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)). Requests filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 are treated by OPAP. If the error is discovered after payment of the issue fee, either withdraw from issue and file RCE with 1.48(f) request or file certificate of correction with a petition under 1.182 after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of name procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an inventor’s name has changed after filing and the inventor desires the change on the application, a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f) with an ADS and processing fee must be submitted; changes cannot be granted after payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is assigned, submit a corrected assignment document with a cover sheet and recording fee (37 CFR 1.21(h)). OPAP handles 1.48(f) requests and will correct Office records and send a corrected filing receipt if compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of joint inventor names and how it is determined
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on/after September 16, 2012, the order of joint patentees in the patent heading is taken from the order in the ADS if submitted before/with the oath/declaration; for applications filed before that date, it is taken from the order in the original oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to change order require 37 CFR 1.48(f) and are treated by OPAP; changes are amendments and cannot be made after payment of the issue fee (37 CFR 1.312). It is suggested that all typewritten and signed names be in the same order as in the oath/declaration at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the application in the oath/declaration (minimum acceptable combinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63 requires an oath/declaration to identify the application. Acceptable minimums when filed on the application filing date include: (A) name of inventor(s) and reference to an attached specification/application that is attached at execution and submitted on filing; (B) name of inventor(s) and attorney docket number on the specification as filed; or (C) name of inventor(s) and title of the invention on the specification as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For oaths/declarations filed after the filing date, additional acceptable combinations (A)-(G) are listed (e.g., application number, serial number and filing date, international application number, attorney docket number, title plus reference to attached spec, or title plus cover letter accurately identifying the application). Variance from these guidelines requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of incorrect identification or misattached oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration attached to a cover letter referencing an incorrect application may not become associated with the correct application and could result in abandonment of the correct application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any variance from identification guidelines only considered upon filing of a waiver petition (37 CFR 1.183) accompanied by the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventorship rules and contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is made by two or more persons jointly, they shall apply for patent jointly and each make the required oath except as otherwise provided. Inventors may apply jointly even though they did not physically work together, did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or did not contribute to the subject matter of every claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple inventors are named in a nonprovisional application, each must have made a contribution to the subject matter of at least one claim; for provisional applications each named inventor must have made a contribution to the subject matter disclosed. Applicants are responsible and required to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48 when claim changes alter inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice may affect inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: If joint inventors' application includes more than one independent and distinct invention, restriction may be required and election of an invention may necessitate changing inventorship if the elected invention was not that of all originally named inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional application complying with 35 U.S.C. 120 may be entitled to benefit of the earlier filing date. Examiner should remind applicants to correct inventorship pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48 if an elected invention results in changes to named inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath or declaration to correct deficiencies (37 CFR 1.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a supplemental inventor's oath or declaration meeting §1.63, §1.64, or §1.162 to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies present in an earlier-filed inventor’s oath or declaration; deficiencies due to failure to meet §1.63(b) may be corrected with an ADS per §1.76 (except inventorship corrections which must be via §1.48).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental oath/declaration must be executed by the person whose oath is being withdrawn, replaced, or otherwise corrected. The Office will not require another oath if one already complies with 35 U.S.C.115 and §1.63 or §1.162. No new matter may be introduced into a nonprovisional application by filing a supplemental oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: When re-execution of oath/declaration is required after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor is not required to re-execute a new oath/declaration after alteration of the application papers provided the changes are minor (e.g., typographical errors, grammatical problems, clarifying sentences) and the statements in the executed declaration remain applicable; if changes would introduce new matter, the inventor should execute a new oath/declaration after reviewing the amended application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.52(c) permits interlineations/alterations so long as the statements in the oath/declaration remain applicable. A substitute specification (§1.125) may be required if the application papers do not comply with §1.52(a) and (b).
